question.prompt: Which one of the following rigid transformations (isometries) maps the line segment \(\overline{AB}\) onto the line segment \(\overline{A'B'}\) so that the image of \(A(-2,1)\) is \(A'(2,-1)\) and the image of \(B(-1,4)\) is \(B'(1,-4)?\)

choices.content:
counterclockwise rotation around the origin by
\(90^\circ\)

translation by \(3\) units to the right and \(5\) units
down

clockwise rotation about the origin by
\(180^\circ\)

solutions.title: Recognize a half-turn
solutions.explanation:
Both coordinates change sign in each prescribed image, which suggests a half-turn about the origin.

A \(180^\circ\) rotation about the origin sends each point to the opposite side of the origin at the same distance. Its coordinate rule is
\[
(x,y)\longmapsto(-x,-y).
\]
Applying this rule gives
\[
A(-2,1)\longmapsto(2,-1)=A',
\qquad
B(-1,4)\longmapsto(1,-4)=B'.
\]
A rotation maps the segment joining two points onto the segment joining their images. Thus the required listed transformation is a clockwise \(\boxed{180^\circ}\) rotation about the origin, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
